GESI capacity building in Manufacturing Africa (PPT, 3.89 MB). An interactive workshop that aims to provide tools and approaches to equip Manufacturing Africa to address key elements. These include:

strategies for success: understanding the business case for gender smart manufacturing

the cost of disregarding social safeguarding: win or lose?

positioning for gender smart investing in practice: show me the money!

Integrating women’s economic empowerment into policies and standards

Gender and acute food insecurity. This report provides a summary of evidence based on a rapid review of literature and 6 interviews, with the aim of supporting FCDO and the wider UK government response to acute food insecurity and famine prevention.

Women’s economic empowerment in Ukraine: key barriers and opportunities since Russia’s full-scale invasion. This is an evidence review on the main economic barriers and opportunities for women in Ukraine.

Trade policy support to women through climate transitions, February 2025. This report examines how the UK’s trade policy can support women in low- and middle-income countries through climate transitions.

Strengthening gender in investment policy reforms in Tanzania, September 2024. This briefing note is aimed at supporting the Government of Tanzania to strengthen economic inclusion within the country’s reforms aimed at foreign and domestic investment.

Strengthening gender in investment policy reforms in Tanzania, October 2023. This work identifies global evidence on how reforms can promote women’s economic empowerment. Also, it identifies entry points for Government of Tanzania to strengthen women’s economic empowerment within the ongoing investment policy reform agenda.

Discriminatory law reform (February 2021) (PDF, 621 KB), Open document text version (ODT,173 KB). Information on how discriminatory laws affect women’s economic empowerment. This includes the lessons about eliminating legal barriers to women’s full and equal participation as employees, managers and business owners.

Macroeconomic policy and women’s economic empowerment during the COVID-19 pandemic (June 2020) (PDF, 874 KB). A snapshot of how COVID-19 economic stimulus measures undertaken by sovereign governments can impact women’s economic empowerment. It provides a brief overview of emergency fiscal and monetary stimulus policy options and their potential impact on women, drawn from examples of responses to previous economic crises.

Taxes and duties for sanitary products in Africa (May 2020) (PDF, 320 KB)Information on the countries in Africa that have removed taxes and duties from sanitary products and the results of these policy decisions, including on the economic empowerment of girls and women.

Women’s economic empowerment and standards and regulatory reform (February 2020) (PDF, 536 KB). A report to provide assistance to UK embassies and high commissions abroad for Product Safety and Standards in the design of interventions for current and future Prosperity Fund programmes.

Todas cuentan en el gobierno local: equidad de género e inclusión social en planes de desarrollo territorial (January 2020) (PDF, 874 KB). A Gender and Inclusion and Women’s Economic Empowerment Toolkit for newly-elected Colombian mayors and governors. It aims to raise awareness and build their capacity on integrating gender and inclusion and women’s economic empowerment into sub-national government policies, plans and projects.

Women’s economic empowerment presentation to newly elected mayors and governors in Colombia (November 2019) (PDF, 2.1 MB). Information to raise awareness and build capacity of newly elected Colombian mayors and governors on gender and inclusion and women’s economic empowerment. It identifies how these can be integrated into sub-national government policies, plans and projects.

Tax and women’s economic empowerment (PDF, 460 KB). Evidence-based arguments for the inclusion of a gender and women’s economic empowerment lens in DFID’s work on tax policy, with case studies.

Labour market including transition from education

Sexual exploitation and harassment in the labour market (May 2023) (PDF, 651 KB), Open document text version (ODT, 827 KB). An evidence review of sexual exploitation and harassment of women and girls during their early careers (‘sex-for-jobs/advancement’).

Women in formal and informal labour markets in Mexico (November 2022) (PDF, 481 KB), Open document text version (ODT, 187 KB)

Women in formal and informal labour markets in Mexico: Spanish version (PDF, 520 KB), Open document text: Spanish version (ODT, 162 KB)

Women in formal and informal labour markets in Mexico: recommendations slides Spanish (PDF, 828 KB). An assessment to strengthen the British Embassy of Mexico’s awareness of why women work in the informal economy in Mexico. It also explores the benefits of women working in the formal economy and the barriers in accessing formal work. The evidence was used by the British Embassy in Mexico in discussions with the Government of Mexico and the Mexican private sector.

Input to terms of reference for a socioeconomic study for TAWDIF II, Algeria (May 2020) (PDF, 318 KB). Assessment of robustness of the terms of reference developed for “socio-economic study on gender in job search and recruitment identification of barriers to women’s economic participation and proposals for corrective actions to stakeholders”. It provides evidence on the barriers that Algerian young women face in transitions from education to decent work. It identifies strategies to overcome these barriers.

Resources on girls’ clubs and self-help impact on women’s economic empowerment, employment and earnings (January 2018) (PDF, 286 KB). An exploration of evidence on the impact of self-help groups and girls’ clubs on livelihoods on employment, earnings, consumption and poverty.

passages.quote:
nagement of business risks and enhanced responsible business practices. It is written for companies or practitioners engaging in GVCs (particularly those in the garment, agriculture and/or personal care sectors) which rely heavily on women workers.

Building back equitably: spotlight on COVID-19 and women workers in global value chains (September 2022) (PDF, 890 KB). This rapid research report builds on the findings of the WOW ‘Hidden in plain sight’ (PDF, 1.7 MB) report. It draws on emerging data about how women workers fared through COVID-19, including women in global value chains. The report argues for proactive strategies by companies and policymakers to rebuild more gender-equal value chains in the COVID-19 recovery. It presents recommendations for achieving this.

The Double Day (July 2020) (PDF, 1.2 MB). In this report, the WOW programme explores the issue of unequal and unpaid work and care among garment workers in Bangladesh. The briefing paper presents an overview of current knowledge about unpaid care in the sector. It shares findings from primary research conducted with garment workers in 2019.

Women and the Net Zero economy: a transition toolkit for businesses with global supply chains (November 2021) (PDF, 982 KB). The transition to Net Zero will impact many of the most vulnerable women working in global supply chains around the world. The WOW programme collaborated with Business Fights Poverty and the Harvard Kennedy School Corporate Responsibility Initiative to create a toolkit for business on gender and climate. It will support businesses to incorporate gender considerations into the action they are taking on climate change throughout their supply chains.

Unpaid and unrecognised: how business can realise the benefits of tackling women’s invisible labour (May 2021) (PDF, 1.2 MB). This guide was developed to support businesses to take tangible steps towards understanding and addressing women’s invisible labour. It explores how businesses rely (both directly and indirectly) on women’s invisible labour for the resilience, productivity and success of their supply chains. Drawing upon real life examples, the report illustrates how business can act on invisible labour and accelerate progress toward a gender-equitable world.

Modern slavery and women’s economic empowerment: a discussion paper (July 2018) (PDF, 1.4 MB). This paper explores how increasing the economic empowerment of women in global value chains can reduce the risk of modern slavery.

Family business management training manual (PDF, 3.16 MB, 84 pages). This detailed curriculum aims to support trainers including local government and NGO staff, to deliver a 5-week couples training course on gender equality and family management of resources. It includes practical exercises to familiarise smallholder famers with issues such as budgeting and valuing productive and non-productive roles equally.

Community dialogues on gender and social norms: facilitation guide for village-based agents (PDF, 15.1 MB, 16 pages). This community engagement guide was developed as part of the WOW partnership with Waitrose, which focused on empowering women in the horticulture supply chain in Kenya. The purpose of the guide is to help Village Based Agents and lead farmers trained by Waitrose’s delivery partner, Farm Africa, to facilitate dialogues within their communities on gender and social norms.

WOW Helpdesk resources

The WOW Helpdesk provided proactive guidance and support on priority themes for women’s economic empowerment across FCDO economic development portfolios. These reports provide advice and information for policymakers, programme designers and implementers.

Climate change and green growth

International Climate Finance and gender equality, portfolio review of FCDO programmes in Tanzania, September 2023. This is a portfolio review of British High Commission Dar Es Salaam programmes, including International Climate Finance components for gender equality.

Integrating gender in the design of scaled-up or new British High Commission Tanzania programmes (March 2024). A summary of entry points for integrating gender equality into the design of 5 British High Commission Dar Es Salaam’s programmes. It addresses how each programme contributes to the 4 pillars of the high commission’s climate and environmental strategy.

Building women’s economic empowerment into climate transitions (March 2024). Pre-reading for an FCDO conference at Wilton Park from 18 to 20 March 2024.

Women’s economic empowerment and climate change (January 2024). An update of the 2021 guidance to help the UK government better understand the differential effects of climate change and support the inclusion of women in climate action. It summarises new evidence and presents a revised framework for action.

Women’s economic empowerment and electric vehicles in Kenya (May 2023) (PDF, 1.2 MB), Open document text version (ODT, 81.4 KB). A review of the status of gender-inclusive design in electric vehicles, with a focus on 2-wheelers and 3-wheelers.

Women’s economic empowerment in the blue economy in Small Island Developing States (February 2023) (PDF, 2 MB), Open document text version (ODT, 197 KB), Women’s economic empowerment in the blue economy in Small Island Developing States, Pacific: slides (ODP, 346 KB), Women’s economic empowerment in the blue economy in Small Island Developing States, Caribbean: slides (ODP, 365 KB). A desk-based review of the evidence on women’s economic empowerment in blue economy sectors in Small Island Developing States where women often take up more precarious, lower paid and less visible jobs. It presents the status, trends and barriers. It looks at how to achieve economic empowerment for more marginalised women. It identifies what works to prevent and respond to violence experienced by women working in these sectors.

Review of women’s economic empowerment and gender work of the business for shared prosperity programme (August 2018) (PDF, 523 KB). A review of gender and women’s economic empowerment inclusion in DFID Burma’s Business for Shared Prosperity Programme.

Commercial agriculture portfolio review: Women’s economic empowerment analysis (July 2018) (PDF, 607 KB). This paper provides an analysis of the gender responsiveness of programmes within the FCDO (then DFID) Commercial Agriculture Team.

Women’s Economic Empowerment and Disability Inclusion in Future Cities programmes (PDF, 212 KB), Open document text version (ODT, 606 KB). A concise summary of current evidence, good practice and resources for integrating the priorities and needs of women and people with disabilities in the Prosperity Fund Global Future Cities programme.

Southern agriculture growth corridor of Tanzania (SAGCOT) strategy review (PDF, 406 KB), Open document text version (ODT, 98.6 KB). Guidance and recommendations on how to better integrate Women’s Economic Empowerment into the 5-year strategy of the Southern Agricultural Growth Corridor of Tanzania Investment Project.

GESI capacity building in Manufacturing Africa (PPT, 3.9 MB). An interactive workshop that aims to provide tools and approaches to equip Manufacturing Africa to address key elements. These include:

strategies for success - understanding the business case for gender smart manufacturing

the cost of disregarding social safeguarding: win or lose?

positioning for gender smart investing in practice: show me the money!

Women’s economic empowerment (general)

Checklist for integrating gender, equality, disability and social inclusion (GEDSI) across FCDO economic development programmes. Guidance on enhancing FCDO support for inclusive growth across different stages of programming, using an adapted economic inclusion framework.

No such thing as a free lunch: investing in and addressing unpaid care and domestic work, the missing component of equitable development (October 2023) (PDF, 3.8 MB). Open document text version (ODT, 1.1 MB). This paper is a reference guide on unpaid care and domestic work for people working in international organisations. It sets out the evidence-base for action. It summarises what initiatives work to ensure that the extent and impacts of unpaid care and domestic work are recognised, reduced and redistributed. The paper demonstrates that there are different ways to address the disproportionate amount of time women spend on unpaid care.

Women’s economic empowerment drivers (March 2023) (PDF, 1.2 MB), Open document text version (ODT, 1.23 MB) , Women’s economic empowerment drivers: slides (ODP, 4.02 MB), UNHLP women’s economic empowerment drivers: infographic (ODT, 229 KB). An evidence review of progress since the UNHLP in 2016 which looks at the latest evidence on the 7 drivers of transformation of women’s economic empowerment.

What works to promote women’s economic empowerment (February 2023) (PDF, 578 KB), Open document text version (ODT, 545KB). An evidence review of the literature on the barriers to women’s economic empowerment and what works to overcome these challenges. It is aimed at UK government staff, particularly those who are not specialists in gender and social development.

Women’s economic empowerment in Côte D’Ivoire (November 2020) (PDF, 515 KB). Information on the reasons behind the economic disparity between men and women in Côte D’Ivoire and the country’s existing economic policies. This is to inform HMG work with the government of Côte D’Ivoire on the design and roll-out of women’s economic empowerment interventions. The findings and recommendations were presented to FCDO in December 2020: WOW Helpdesk Query 57 (MS PowerPoint Presentation, 1.4 MB).

International financial institutions and women’s economic empowerment (October 2022) (PDF, 884 KB), Open document text version (ODT, 717 KB). A mapping and critical assessment of the work carried out by International Financial Institutions on women’s economic empowerment. This assessment enabled FCDO to engage with the World Bank Group as it launched a refresh of their gender strategy.

Promoting economic empowerment for women in the informal economy (September 2019) (PDF, 969 KB). This paper provides an analysis of the gender dynamics of informal work, and a set of corresponding recommendations to promote better jobs for women. It is aimed at FCDO and UK government advisers working on economic development, across a range of issues. These include agriculture, business environment, private sector development, social protection, urban and infrastructure development, digital development and research.

Women workers in global value chains: a research briefing (July 2018) (PDF, 245 KB). This paper provides an overview of WOW research on the role and work of women in global value chains.

Women’s economic empowerment and disability inclusion in financial services (PDF, 418 KB), Open document text version (ODT, 270KB). A rapid review of evidence, good practice and resources for integrating the priorities and needs of women and people with disabilities in the finance sector and economic development programmes.

Evidence digests

The WOW Helpdesk provides regular updates which are distributed across the FCDO network. They collate learning and information from the WOW programme and signpost to new resources on women’s economic empowerment.

Evidence digest: September 2024 (ODP, 917 KB):

targeted guidance on measurement of women’s economic empowerment
